To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

chemotherapy consisting of CAP-1 as an adjunct to primary surgery in stage I and II epithelial ovarian carcinoma results in a high rate of complete remission, but that the overall relapse rate is still high.
the use of CAP-1 chemotherapy in stage Ic or stage II ovarian cancer patients resulted in a relapse rate of 40% (9/25) and a 5-year survival rate of 60% (95% CI 39-80%) in all patients.

the addition of cisplatin-based systemic chemotherapy following surgery for stage Ic-II (early stage) epithelial ovarian cancer is associated with an overall relapse rate of 40% at 5 years, with a median follow-up of all 25 patients of 5 years.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of chemotherapy as an adjunct to surgical treatment in stage Ic and II ovarian cancer.
the development of new methods for the treatment of cancer and the improvement of the quality of life of patients with cancer.
the treatment of stage Ic-II (early) epithelial ovarian cancer with surgery combined with CAP-1 chemotherapy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CAP-1 is a promising regimen in early stage ovarian cancer and that a randomized trial should be performed to confirm the efficacy of this regimen in comparison to other regimens.
CAP-1 is a reasonable treatment for patients with stage I-II epithelial ovarian cancer.

the use of chemotherapy as an adjunct to optimal surgical treatment of early stage ovarian cancer appears to be at the least as good as postoperative radiotherapy or intraperitoneally radioactive phosphorus.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the combination chemotherapy CAP-1, as an adjunct to total tumor removal, may be an effective treatment for patients with stage I-II epithelial ovarian cancer.

the use of cisplatin based combination chemotherapy as an adjuvant treatment to surgery is an effective treatment for early stage ovarian carcinoma and is at least equivalent to other treatment modalities.
chemotherapy is a good option in early stage ovarian cancer.
The main takeaway from our work is that
cisplatin-based combination chemotherapy is an effective adjuvant treatment for patients with stage I-II epithelial ovarian cancer.
the use of cisplatin-containing chemotherapy in the adjuvant setting for early-stage ovarian cancer is safe and effective.
the addition of cisplatin to doxorubicin plus cyclophosphomide chemotherapy is feasible in patients with stage I-II epithelial ovarian cancer.
